pr_body:
This does the following:
- rename `enum udev_builtin_cmd` -> `UdevBuiltinCmd`
- rename `struct udev_builtin` -> `UdevBuiltin`
- move type definitions to udev-rules.h
- move prototypes of functions defined in udev-rules.c to udev-rules.h
- drop to use `strbuf`
- propagate critical errors in applying rules
- drop limitation for number of tokens per line

This also adds `--evaluate-run=early|late` command line option for `udevd`. Closes #12291.
pr_comments:
I don't think this is a good approach. Having two modes of execution, switchable by a commandline switch would mean that all rules would have to be compatible with both modes. Let's just pick a behaviour and stick to it.

The docs say that RESULT and $result/%c are from PROGRAM. They don't specify which one. I think it's reasonable to assume that this means the last one that precedes the use of $result/%c/RESULT. I'd clarify this in the docs.

I'd treat current behaviour as a bug. It means that the effect of a rule can be completely changed by another later rule, which makes everything completely unpredictable and useless.
@keszybz Yeah, the second patch is quite huge, and I understand it is hard to review. I will try to split the commit.

issue_context.title: udev: RUN assignments and PROGRAM results
issue_context.body:
This bug report is based on the latest sourcecode of udev, I had a really hard time to debug my [udev rule](https://github.com/atar-axis/xpadneo/issues/91) and therefore had a closer look into the sourcecode.

**The first set of issues is about the `RUN` key**

Problematic code: [here](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/15de23a0b24f6073d527c6a8c22556ad5101a160/src/udev/udev-rules.c#L2442)

1. <strike>Final assignments on the `RUN` key cannot work. This is because `event->run_final` exists, but is never set or checked. I therefore suggest to add the following:
    ```
    if (event->run_final)
        break;
    if (cur->key.op == OP_ASSIGN_FINAL)
        event->run_final = true;
    ```
    If this behaviour is intended, then please document it :blush:
   </strike> (fixed by [PR](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/12309))

2. <strike>Using `=` or `:=` on the `RUN{builtin}` key does clear the whole `event->run_list`, even `RUN{program}` entries (and vice versa). This is not documented either. I suggest to separate both `RUN` commands or documenting this behaviour.</strike> (fixed by [PR](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/12310))

3. <strike>It should be documented that `RUN` commands are not executed sequentially</strike> (fixed by https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/11891/commits/541d8bd4b18a4b97a381ae6caea4aba2baaa063c)


**The next issue is about the `PROGRAM` and `RESULT` keys**

Imagine the following situation:
* You have two different rules, both fire on the same uevent.
* Both rules have an `PROGRAM` command and both are using the `$result` variable in their `RUN` commands.

Now the problem is, that the `PROGRAM` commands are executed before the `RUN` commands, meaning that the second rule is overriding the `$result` of the first one.
Therefore the `RUN` command of the first rule does now have the `$result` of `PROGRAM` of the second rule.

I suggest to evaluate `PROGRAM` first and replacing the `$result` variable in `RUN` commands before it gets added to the `event->run_list`. At the moment the substitution does happen shortly before execution, see [here](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/3661dc349ec0e0e8f19fb3a542ccbc813753ef8b/src/udev/udev-event.c#L907). Otherwise, please document this behaviour! :relaxed:

Hum, I would think that backwards compatibility is not a thing here because this behaviour is absolutely not what you would expect. Not changing that feels like keeping a bug because some ppl. already implemented a workaround.

Anyhow, if you don't want to change that, then we should at least document it, right? 😊
I've posted a commit in #12416 which adds an option to evaluate `RUN=` rules earlier. PTAL.

Ah nice, thank you for the information! But Is there a way to determine which one (early/late) is set? For someone who delivers udev rules this adds even more uncertainty of how the rule is executed :) there should be exactly one way in my eyes, and this one should be documented :)
Thank you for the comments. I will add a log message about the option, and update man page.

Thanks! So then I think this issue is completely covered now :grin:

Btw, wouldn't it be better to set the early/late thingy "per rule" (something like `RUN_EVAL=EARLY`)? I think that's most probably more complicated to implement, but it would guarantee backwards compatibility (if it defaults to `LATE`), it would be easier to determine the behaviour and it would allow rule-providers to set it "as desired"

review_comments: Yep, this seems to work exactly as I would expect.
